faq.q: Why do we need to drink water?
faq.a: We lose water all day through breath, sweat and wee. Water carries food and oxygen in our blood, cools us with sweat and keeps our brain and body working, so we need to keep topping it up.

faq.q: How much of my body is water?
faq.a: About 60 percent of an adult's body is water. Children have a bit more, around 65 percent, and babies about 75 percent.
asks: Is my body made of water?

faq.q: What happens if I do not drink enough?
faq.a: You become dehydrated, which means short of water. You may feel thirsty, tired, dizzy or grumpy, get a headache, and your wee turns dark yellow.

faq.q: How do I know if I am drinking enough?
faq.a: A simple check is the colour of your wee: pale yellow is good, dark yellow means drink more. Drink more on hot days and when you exercise.
asks: How much water should I drink?

faq.q: Do other drinks count as water?
faq.a: Milk, soup and fruit like watermelon all give you water. Sugary drinks give water too but are bad for teeth, so plain water is the best choice.
asks: Is juice as good as water?

facts: Water makes up about 60 percent of an adult's body weight and about 75 percent of a newborn baby's.
People can survive only a few days without water, compared with weeks without food.

quiz.why: As sweat dries on your skin, it carries heat away and cools you.

quiz.why: Dark yellow wee is a sign you need more water.
